free_tier.stated: unverified: no free tier, free credit or trial is stated on the pricing page read on 2026-11-25; the page says 'No setup fees, no monthly minimums. Pay only for what you use.' Compute is $0.38 per core-hour and $0.095 per GiB-hour, billed per second, and a normal browser workload runs at roughly $0.075/hour
free_tier.notes: The provider list's '$1.14/h' and '4.5 h free (one time)' figures are not on any first-party page read and are not asserted here. The hosted API also bills model tokens separately: northstar-cua-fast-1.6 is $0.50/M input and $1.50/M output, with about 1,974 fixed extra input tokens per computer-use step.

per_object_cap.stated: uploads to a desktop session go to /workspace/uploads, up to 512 MB per file, transferred in 8 MB chunks; no account-wide file cap is stated

retention.stated: unverified: no workspace-file retention period after a session terminates is stated on the pages read; screenshot URLs are presigned and expire after about 7 days; sessions can be saved with persistent=True and restored

egress.terms: not published as a per-GB price: compute bills at $0.38/core-hour of actual core usage and $0.095/GiB-hour of actual memory used; no outbound byte allowance or price per GB is stated on the pages read. Google domains and chrome:// URLs are blocked in browser sessions, and browser downloads are disabled.

record.interface_detail: An HTTP API and Python/TypeScript SDKs (pip install tzafon) for tasks, computers and Responses/Chat Completions, plus a CLI. A computer session is a sandboxed browser or desktop that Northstar operates; a live view exists at https://lightcone.ai/c/{computer_id}.
record.tooling: A hosted API and Python/TypeScript SDKs; a CLI for tasks and computers. The northstar-cua-fast model weights are Apache 2.0 and can be run by the user on their own machine, and lightcone.ai/platform offers VPC, on-prem and self-hosted deployment; these are listed last and are not the hosted offer priced here.
record.chaining: A hosted computer session can run a browser or desktop at roughly $0.075/hour of compute plus model tokens, so a computer-use agent pays per step; files that must outlive a session are saved with persistent=True, and a self-hosted model on the user's own machine is the last-resort alternative when no hosted run is wanted.

limits.value: sessions terminate after inactivity_timeout_seconds and a hard max_lifetime_seconds always applies regardless of activity
concurrent computers are plan-dependent; exceeding the limit returns 429 'Concurrent limit reached'
512 MB per uploaded file, transferred in 8 MB chunks, to /workspace/uploads

record.limits_note: Compute bills per second, minimum 0.125 cores per container; desktop uploads have no download action, so small files are returned via shell stdout. Browser sessions allow at most 5 tabs, block Google domains and chrome:// URLs, and deny downloads.
record.binding_note: A session's inactivity timeout and hard max lifetime end the billed computer before a plan-level concurrent limit or the 512 MB upload cap is reached in a normal computer-use task.

identity_cost.detail: The hosted sign-in at login.tzafon.ai (WorkOS AuthKit) asks for 'Email' with 'Continue with email', and offers 'Continue with Google', 'Continue with GitHub' and 'Continue with Apple'; a probe of the sign-in page captured the form on 2026-11-25. No card, phone or ID is asked for on that page; whether a card is needed before a paid computer can start is unverified: behind a sign-up.

record.reliability_note: Sessions are reaped after an inactivity timeout and a hard lifetime cap; concurrent computers are plan-dependent with a 429 on overrun; browser sessions block Google domains and chrome:// URLs and deny downloads; screenshot links expire after about 7 days.
record.confidence_note: Compute rates, token rates, no-fee statement and file/session limits are quoted from the first-party docs.lightcone.ai pricing and limits pages read on 2026-11-25; the identity gate was read from a probe of the WorkOS sign-in page reached from lightcone.ai/dashboard.

egress.terms: not published: the pricing page lists token, CPU, memory and disk rates with no outbound transfer allowance or per-GB price; browser sessions support a residential proxy option, desktop sessions do not

record.interface_detail: Tasks, Responses API and Chat Completions over REST, a `lightcone` CLI and MCP server, a chat interface, cloud browsers driven through CDP/Playwright, and shell commands on a desktop session; the SDKs are Python (`tzafon`) and TypeScript (`@tzafon/lightcone`).
record.tooling: pip install tzafon, npm install @tzafon/lightcone, the lightcone CLI and MCP server; Playwright or Puppeteer can attach to browser sessions over CDP.
record.chaining: Runs Northstar computer-use tasks on a managed cloud desktop or browser and returns screenshots and HTML to the caller; hosted only, with an on-device Mac option named last in the platform docs and no own hardware required.

limits.value: CPU $0.38 per core-hour and memory $0.095 per GiB-hour, billed per second with a minimum of 0.125 cores per container

record.limits_note: Browser sessions allow at most 5 tabs, block downloads and Google domains, and cache html() for about 2 seconds; desktop session actions are serialized one at a time.
record.binding_note: No free allowance is published, so the meter starts at first use: a typical browser workload is about $0.075 an hour and a 10-20-step task lands between a few cents and about $0.50.

identity_cost.detail: The signup page presents an email field ('Your email address') and Continue with Google, GitHub and Apple; the quickstart says to sign up at lightcone.ai and copy an API key from the dashboard. No card, phone or ID is shown on signup, and the dashboard is behind a login wall, so any card requirement after signup is unverified: behind a sign-up.

record.reliability_note: Idle sessions are reaped and a hard lifetime cap applies regardless of activity; exceeding the concurrent computer limit returns 429; 10 failed authentication attempts in 10 minutes block the source IP. The API and SDK are in beta and behavior can change.
record.confidence_note: The rates, no-minimum statement, caps, timeouts and signup fields are quoted from first-party documentation read on 2026-11-24; the absence of a published free tier is on the pricing page, and the dashboard was a login wall.
